documents.content:
Location: Chungthang
District: Mangan (North Sikkim)
Risk Type: Flood / GLOF
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: Chungthang lies in the Teesta basin and was a major impact area during the 4 Oct 2023 South Lhonak GLOF. SSDMA's post-disaster assessment also places the Chungthang region in medium-high to very-high multi-hazard zones.
Warning Signs: Rapid rise in river level; intense/prolonged rainfall; official flood/GLOF warnings; unusual debris-laden river flow.
Safety Precautions: Move away from river banks and low-lying areas; follow official alerts; do not cross flood water; evacuate to higher/safe ground if instructed.
Approximate Risk Reduction: No fixed safe time. Immediate risk reduces only after river levels/rainfall subside and authorities issue an all-clear; underlying flood/GLOF risk remains.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use officially opened higher-ground shelters/routes; avoid Teesta river-bank roads and damaged bridges until cleared.

metadata.official_document_section: PDNA → SIKKIM PDNA (2023 GLOF); check Roads & Transport / Chungthang impact section
metadata.verification_note: Official Government of Sikkim SSDMA source. Open Resources page and click PDNA.

documents.content:
Location: Mangan Town
District: Mangan (North Sikkim)
Risk Type: Landslide
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA states that recurring landslide issues affect the SNT site in Mangan town and has initiated a pilot mitigation project with NDMA support. The work includes slope stabilization and drainage measures, showing that the area requires active landslide-risk management.
Warning Signs: Continuous heavy rain; fresh cracks; falling stones/debris; blocked drains/jhoras; unusual slope movement or muddy runoff.
Safety Precautions: Follow weather advisories; move away from slide paths and steep slopes; avoid blocked/affected roads; use only routes cleared by local authorities.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term danger may fall after heavy rain stops and slope/road inspection is completed, but recurring monsoon landslide risk remains.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use authority-approved diversion/open road; move toward stable open areas away from active slide paths.

metadata.official_document_section: Pilot Project for Landslide Mitigation at Mangan (SNT Site)
metadata.verification_note: Official SSDMA activity page directly states recurring landslide issues at Mangan SNT site.

documents.content:
Location: 7th Mile, Gangtok–Tsomgo Road
District: Gangtok / East Sikkim
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA's landslide inventory identifies the 7th Mile Gangtok–Tsomgo Road slide as an old perennial slide. Documented triggers include steep slope, sheared rocks and water, with road damage noted.
Warning Signs: Rock/debris fall; cracks or fresh material on road; heavy rain; water seepage; traffic/road closure notices.
Safety Precautions: Avoid stopping below unstable slopes; follow road-closure instructions; do not cross fresh debris; stay alert during heavy rain and use only cleared routes.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Event risk may reduce after rainfall eases and debris/slope is inspected and cleared; the site remains a perennial landslide location.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use an officially announced diversion or postpone travel if the J.N. Road/Tsomgo route is closed.

District: East Sikkim (source classification)

Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA's landslide inventory describes Jitlang Slide at Rangpo as an old, complex and perennial slide. The site has faulted/sheared rock and steep-slope conditions, with recorded damage to NH 31A and habitation.
Warning Signs: Fresh cracks or slope movement; falling rock/debris; blocked drainage; heavy rain; official road/landslide warning.
Safety Precautions: Keep away from the slide path and unstable slopes; follow official road closures; do not cross fresh debris; move to a stable open/safe area if authorities advise evacuation.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate danger may reduce after rainfall stops, drainage/slope conditions stabilize and authorities inspect/clear the road. The underlying site remains a perennial landslide hazard.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use only an authority-approved diversion/open route around Rangpo; avoid the affected NH corridor until clearance.

Location: Lower Tintek Marchak (Dikchu–Singtam corridor)
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA records this site as an old perennial debris-avalanche slide. Weak geology, excessive rainfall and unmanaged drainage are listed triggers; past damage included road, houses and agricultural land.
Warning Signs: Intense/prolonged rain; muddy runoff; falling boulders/debris; new cracks; drain overflow; road blockage.
Safety Precautions: Avoid the affected slope and road section; follow local traffic restrictions; move away from drainage channels and slide paths; use only routes declared open by authorities.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term risk may reduce after heavy rainfall ends, drainage flow normalizes and the slope/road is inspected. Recurrence remains possible because the site is classified as perennial.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use an officially announced Dikchu–Singtam diversion when available; otherwise delay travel until the road is cleared.

District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA's inventory identifies 2nd Mile Kumrek as an old perennial complex slide. Adverse geology, steep slope and toe cutting are listed as triggers, with recorded damage to road and forest.

Safety Precautions: Do not stop below unstable cut slopes; obey closures; avoid crossing active debris; remain alert during rain and use only cleared road sections.

documents.content:
Location: Chandmari, Gangtok
District: Gangtok District
Risk Type: Landslide
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA operates a real-time landslide early-warning system at Chandmari. Sensors monitor ground movement and moisture and are used to identify threshold conditions for potential landslides, indicating a location requiring active landslide monitoring.
Warning Signs: Official early-warning alert; abnormal ground movement; increasing soil moisture after heavy rain; fresh cracks; small rock/soil falls.
Safety Precautions: Follow official warnings immediately; move away from unstable slopes/slide paths; stay alert during heavy rainfall; evacuate to a designated safe area if instructed.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term danger may reduce when rainfall stops, sensor readings return to stable levels and authorities withdraw the warning. No fixed safe time should be assumed.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Move to an officially designated stable/open safe area; use only local routes confirmed open by authorities.

metadata.official_document_section: Real-Time Landslide Early Warning System – Chandmari, Gangtok
metadata.verification_note: Official SSDMA activity page documents the real-time early-warning system at Chandmari.

documents.content:
Location: South Lhonak Glacial Lake / downstream Teesta corridor
District: Mangan (North Sikkim)
Risk Type: Flood / GLOF
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: South Lhonak is a critical glacial lake monitored for GLOF risk. It was associated with the 4 October 2023 GLOF disaster that severely affected downstream Teesta-valley areas, so sudden lake outburst and downstream flood propagation are key hazards.
Warning Signs: Official GLOF/flood alert; unusual lake or river-level rise; intense precipitation; sudden debris-laden flow; evacuation warnings for downstream areas.
Safety Precautions: Move to higher ground away from river channels and low-lying flood zones; follow SSDMA/local authority alerts; never attempt to cross fast flood water; evacuate when instructed.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate downstream danger may reduce only after lake/river monitoring stabilizes and authorities issue an all-clear. The long-term GLOF hazard cannot be assigned a fixed end time.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use designated higher-ground shelters/routes and avoid the Teesta river corridor or damaged bridges until authorities confirm safe access.

Location: 13th Mile Slide, J.N. Road
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA's landslide inventory records the 13th Mile slide on J.N. Road as an old active landslide. It is associated with steep slope conditions, downslope-dipping rock foliation, freeze-thaw action and rainwater, with J.N. Road listed as damaged infrastructure.
Warning Signs: Heavy/prolonged rain; fresh rock or debris fall; cracks/subsidence near the road; unusual slope movement; official road warning or closure.
Safety Precautions: Avoid stopping below unstable slopes; follow road-closure instructions; do not cross fresh debris; keep away from active slide zones and use only routes cleared by authorities.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate travel risk may reduce after rainfall stops, slope movement stabilizes and authorities inspect/clear the road. The site remains an active recorded landslide location.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use only an officially opened diversion; postpone J.N. Road travel if the affected section is closed.

Approximate Risk Reduction: Event-level danger may reduce after slope conditions stabilize and inspection/clearance is completed. Long-term susceptibility remains because the slide is recorded as perennial.

Location: Kyongsla Slide, J.N. Road (15th Mile)
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA records Kyongsla Slide on J.N. Road (15th Mile) as a block-and-wedge failure in jointed gneiss within a shear zone. Steep slope, jointed/sheared rock and vibration are listed triggers, with J.N. Road damage and a return period described as perennial unless corrected.
Warning Signs: Falling boulders/rock; fresh fractures; debris on road; slope movement; heavy rain or vibration; official closure warning.
Safety Precautions: Keep clear of the rock-fall zone; do not stop below unstable slopes; obey closures; cross the area only after official inspection and clearance.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term risk may reduce after active movement stops and the road/slope is cleared. The recorded hazard can recur unless corrective stabilization is completed.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Follow an officially announced diversion or postpone travel on the affected J.N. Road section.

documents.content:
Location: Singtam, Teesta River Corridor
District: Gangtok District
Risk Type: Flood / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: Official SSDMA records from the October 2023 Teesta-basin flood document major impacts in Singtam, including a washed-out bridge, extensive NH-10 damage, damaged sewage infrastructure and submergence of power-related facilities. This demonstrates high exposure of low-lying river-corridor infrastructure to severe flood events.
Warning Signs: Rapid Teesta water-level rise; intense rainfall or upstream flood/GLOF alert; debris-laden water; bridge/road closure; evacuation warning.
Safety Precautions: Move to higher ground away from the river and low-lying areas; follow official alerts; never cross floodwater; avoid damaged bridges and NH sections until authorities reopen them.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate risk reduces only after river levels fall, rainfall/upstream alerts ease and authorities issue an all-clear. There is no fixed safe-time estimate for a severe flood event.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use designated higher-ground shelters and only routes officially declared open; avoid the Teesta riverbank/NH-10 affected stretch during an active alert.

metadata.official_document_section: Sikkim GLOF Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) 2023 → search 'Singtam'; also SSDMA flood damage report dated 19 Oct 2023
metadata.verification_note: Official Government of Sikkim SSDMA records document 2023 flood damage in Singtam. Dataset rating is historical-risk classification, not a current alert.

documents.content:
Location: Rangpo, Teesta River Corridor
District: Pakyong District
Risk Type: Flood / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA's official October 2023 flood-damage record states that Rangpo and nearby areas were severely affected, with NH-10 damage, submerged facilities and riverside habitations, plus extensive infrastructure damage. This indicates significant flood and transport exposure along the Teesta corridor.
Warning Signs: Rapid river rise; official flood/GLOF warning; intense rainfall; water/debris entering riverside areas; NH-10 closure or bridge/utility disruption.
Safety Precautions: Move away from riverbanks and low-lying areas; follow evacuation directions; never drive through floodwater; avoid NH-10 and damaged infrastructure until officially cleared.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate danger may reduce after Teesta levels fall and authorities confirm that roads, bridges and utilities are safe. Long-term flood exposure remains and has no fixed end time.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use higher-ground safe areas and authority-approved alternate routes; avoid the Teesta/NH-10 corridor during an active warning.

metadata.official_document_section: Sikkim GLOF Post Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) 2023 → search 'Rangpo'; also SSDMA flood damage report dated 19 Oct 2023
metadata.verification_note: Official SSDMA records document severe 2023 flood impacts in Rangpo. 'High' is a Bhudrishti research classification, not a live alert.

Location: Bordang Slide on Rangpo–Singtam Road
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA records Bordang as an old, active complex landslide on the Rangpo–Singtam road. The site has sheared Daling-formation rock fragments and a steep slope; NH 31A is listed as damaged. The inventory identifies adverse geology and steep slope as the main triggers.
Warning Signs: Fresh rock/soil fall; cracks or deformation on the road edge; unusual slope movement; debris after rain; official road restriction or closure.
Safety Precautions: Keep away from the active slope and fresh debris; obey road closures; do not stop below unstable cut slopes; use only road sections that authorities have inspected and reopened.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term travel risk may reduce after active movement stops and the road/slope is inspected and cleared. Because SSDMA lists the slide as active, susceptibility should not be treated as permanently removed.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: No specific alternate route is verified in the source; use only an authority-approved diversion/open route.

documents.content:
Location: Gantey, West Pendam (Singtam–Pendam Road)
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA describes Gantey, West Pendam as a large subsidence/rotational slide with thick slope material and excessive groundwater. Recorded impacts include road, agricultural land, forest and habitation, indicating both transport and settlement exposure.
Warning Signs: Ground cracks or sinking; tilted/uneven road surface; seepage or unusually wet ground; boulder/soil movement; worsening conditions after prolonged rain.
Safety Precautions: Move away from visibly subsiding ground and unstable slopes; avoid affected road sections; follow evacuation/traffic instructions; keep drainage paths clear where safe to do so.
Approximate Risk Reduction: There is no reliable fixed recovery time. SSDMA notes no return estimate considering the size of the subsidence; immediate risk should be considered reduced only after ground movement and water conditions stabilize and authorities inspect the site.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: No official alternate route is specified in the inventory; follow local authority diversions.

documents.content:
Location: Padamchen Slide
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA identifies Padamchen as an old perennial rotational slide involving jointed quartzite, phyllite, rock fragments, soil and large boulders. Recorded damage includes road and agricultural land; triggers include adverse geology, quarrying, steep slope and groundwater.
Warning Signs: Fresh boulders/rock fragments; widening cracks; seepage; fresh scarps; debris on the road; increased activity after rain or slope cutting.
Safety Precautions: Avoid the slide path and unstable quarry/slope areas; do not cross fresh debris; obey road closures; travel only after official inspection and clearance.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Immediate risk may reduce after groundwater/rain conditions ease and no new movement is observed, followed by official clearance. SSDMA lists the slide as perennial, so long-term susceptibility remains.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: No specific safe route is given in the official inventory; use an authority-approved diversion or delay travel.

Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA records Namcheybong as an old perennial complex/translational slide. Bedrock dips downslope and the site has strong surface/sub-surface water activity. Damage is recorded to agricultural land, houses, forest and road.
Warning Signs: New ground or wall cracks; slope bulging; increased seepage; muddy runoff; road deformation; small debris falls that may precede larger movement.
Safety Precautions: Move away from the slide path and unstable buildings/slopes; avoid affected roads; follow local evacuation instructions; do not enter areas with active cracking or debris movement.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term danger may reduce after groundwater levels and rainfall decrease and the slope is inspected as stable. SSDMA classifies the site as perennial, so risk can recur.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use only routes declared open by authorities; no site-specific alternate route is verified in the source.

District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA identifies the Pegay slide as a perennial wedge-type failure on the Pakyong–Linkey road. Joint failure, underground water, steep slope and adverse geology are listed as triggers, while the road and forest are recorded as damaged.
Warning Signs: Rock wedges or fragments detaching; fresh debris; seepage; cracks along rock joints; road blockage or deformation, especially after rainfall.
Safety Precautions: Stay clear of rock-fall zones; do not stop below unstable rock faces; follow closures; cross the section only after official inspection and reopening.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Event-level danger may reduce once water conditions and rock movement stabilize and debris is cleared. Perennial classification means recurrence remains possible.

District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Rock-fall Risk
Risk Level: Medium
Risk Reason: SSDMA records Rangchang Khola at Tumin as a recent rock-fall site in quartzite/phyllite terrain. Weak geology, steep slope and rainfall are listed triggers. The inventory records forest impact and specifically notes no impact on habitation.
Warning Signs: Fresh rock fragments below the slope; isolated boulder fall; new cracks in exposed rock; increased fall activity during or after rain.
Safety Precautions: Keep away from the base of steep rock faces; avoid stopping in rock-fall paths; follow local warnings and move through affected road/slope areas only if officially cleared.
Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term risk may reduce after rainfall stops and no further rock fall is observed. Because the inventory describes a recent event rather than a verified permanently stabilized site, caution remains appropriate.

Location: Tsochen–Pheri Slide
District: East Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA documents Tsochen–Pheri as a very large perennial complex slide in sheared/rotated gneissic terrain. The inventory records road cut-off since 1997 along with impacts to agricultural land, habitation and forest; adverse geology and high water regime are listed triggers.
Warning Signs: Persistent ground movement; road cracking or collapse; large boulder/debris movement; strong seepage; renewed instability during prolonged wet periods.
Safety Precautions: Avoid the active slide mass and closed road; move away from unstable buildings/slopes; follow evacuation and traffic restrictions; do not attempt to cross a cut-off or freshly failed road.
Approximate Risk Reduction: No fixed recovery time should be assumed. Immediate access risk may fall only after movement/water conditions stabilize and engineering/authority inspection confirms safety; SSDMA lists the site as perennial.
Alternative Safe Location or Route: Use only officially announced alternate access; do not improvise routes across the slide area.

District: East Sikkim (source classification)

Risk Level: High

Approximate Risk Reduction: Short-term danger may reduce if ground movement and groundwater conditions stabilize and the area is inspected. SSDMA lists the subsidence as perennial, so long-term recurrence remains possible.

Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA describes Doksing as a perennial wedge-type landslide in adverse Daling-group geology. The documented slide extends roughly 2 km and has damaged the Rongli–Rhenock road; steep slope and fractured rock are listed triggers.

documents.content:
Location: Mangshila Slide
District: North Sikkim (source classification)
Risk Type: Landslide / Road & Settlement Risk
Risk Level: High
Risk Reason: SSDMA records Mangshila as an old debris slide in a highly disturbed geological formation. Agricultural land, road and houses are listed as damaged, while bad geology and high groundwater/rainwater are identified as triggers.
